cohort: The study included 85 pregnant women diagnosed with cardiac disease who were followed throughout their antenatal, delivery, and postpartum periods.
finding: Rheumatic heart disease was the most common cardiac condition (40%) complicating pregnancies, and cardiac complications were observed in 10% of cases, while all pregnancies resulted in live births with a mean birth weight of 2.8 kg.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the predominant mode of delivery (55%) in this cohort.
